claims.text: The proposed hallucination detection method combines Jaccard similarity for entity-level alignment, natural language inference for semantic consistency, and normalized perplexity for fluency via a weighted average.
In the proposed detection framework, a higher metric score corresponds to a higher likelihood of hallucination in generated text.

evidence.description: The method combines three complementary components: Jaccard similarity for entity-level alignment, natural language inference for semantic consistency, and a normalized perplexity measure for fluency through a weighted average.
The integration of these components through a weighted average produces a hallucination metric where a high value indicates a potential occurrence of hallucination.

methodologies.name: Weighted Multi-Component Hallucination Metric
methodologies.description: A metric-based hallucination detection approach integrating Jaccard similarity, natural language inference, and normalized perplexity via a weighted average.

limitations.text: Large language models frequently generate content that is fabricated and factually incorrect.
